title: Create a project
body:
Every piece of work in Harbour Projects lives in a project.
1. In the left sidebar, select **Projects**.
2. Select **New project**.
3. Enter a **Project name** and, if you like, a short **Description**.
4. Choose a **Start date** and **Due date**.
5. Select **Create project**.
The project opens on its **Overview** tab, ready for tasks.

title: Create a project from a template
aliases: use a template for a new project
body:
Templates save you rebuilding the same tasks and columns each time.
1. Select **Projects** in the left sidebar.
2. Select the arrow next to **New project**, then choose **From template**.
3. Pick a template from the **Template library**.
4. Enter a **Project name** and set the **Start date**. Task dates shift to match.
5. Select **Create project**.

title: Save a project as a template
aliases: make a template from a project
body:
Save a project you are happy with so your team can reuse its tasks, columns and settings.
1. Open the project and select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top right.
2. Select **Save as template**.
3. Enter a **Template name**.
4. Choose whether to **Include tasks** and **Include files**.
5. Select **Save template**.
Comments and time logs are never copied into a template.

title: Rename a project
body:
1. Open the project.
2. Select the **Settings** tab.
3. Under **General**, edit the **Project name** field.
4. Select **Save changes**.
The new name appears straight away in the sidebar, in reports and on any task notifications sent from now on. Old notifications keep the previous name.

title: Edit a project description
aliases: add a description to a project
body:
The description sits at the top of the **Overview** tab and helps new members understand the project.
1. Open the project and select the **Overview** tab.
2. Select **Edit description**.
3. Type or paste your text. You can use bold and bullet lists.
4. Select **Save**.
Guests with access to the project can read the description too.

title: Change a project’s start and due dates
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Under **Schedule**, select the **Start date** or **Due date** field.
3. Choose the new date from the calendar.
4. To move tasks with the project, tick **Shift task dates by the same amount**.
5. Select **Save changes**.
Tasks that now fall outside the project dates are flagged with an amber warning on the **Timeline**.

title: Change a project’s status
body:
Status tells your team and clients where a project stands.
1. Open the project.
2. Select the status badge next to the project name, for example **On track**.
3. Choose **On track**, **At risk**, **Off track**, **On hold** or **Complete**.
4. Add a short note if you wish.
5. Select **Update status**.
Each change is recorded in the **Status history** on the **Overview** tab.

title: Post a project status update
aliases: add a progress note to a project
body:
Status updates give stakeholders a written summary without a meeting.
1. Open the project and select the **Overview** tab.
2. Select **New update**.
3. Choose a **Status** and write your summary.
4. Tick **Notify guests** if clients should receive it.
5. Select **Post update**.
Project members get an email and an in-app notification.

title: Archive a project
body:
Archiving removes a project from your active list but keeps everything in it.
1. Open the project.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Archive project**.
3. Select **Archive** to confirm.
Archived projects are read-only. Members and guests can still view them, but nobody can add tasks or comments until the project is restored.

title: Restore an archived project
body:
1. Select **Projects** in the left sidebar.
2. Select the **Filter** button and choose **Archived**.
3. Open the project you want to bring back.
4. Select **Restore project** at the top of the page.
5. Choose a status, such as **On track**, then select **Restore**.
The project returns to your active list with all tasks, files and comments intact.

title: Delete a project
body:
Only project owners and account admins can delete a project. Deleting is permanent after 30 days.
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Scroll to **Danger zone**.
3. Select **Delete project**.
4. Type the project name to confirm.
5. Select **Delete forever**.
If you may want the work later, archive the project instead.

title: Duplicate a project
aliases: make a copy of an existing project
body:
1. Select **Projects** in the left sidebar.
2. Hover over the project and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Duplicate**.
4. Enter a name for the copy.
5. Choose what to include: **Tasks**, **Files**, **Members** and **Board layout**.
6. Select **Duplicate project**.
Comments and time logs are not copied. Use a template if you plan to repeat this often.

title: Export a project’s tasks to CSV
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) above the task list.
3. Select **Export to CSV**.
4. Choose the columns you need, such as **Assignee**, **Due date** and **Status**.
5. Select **Export**.
The file downloads to your browser’s usual download folder. Subtasks appear on their own rows.

title: Add a team member to a project
aliases: invite a colleague to a project
give someone access to a project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Select **Add member**.
3. Start typing the person’s name or email address and choose them from the list.
4. Pick a **Role**: **Manager**, **Contributor** or **Viewer**.
5. Select **Add**.
They receive a notification and the project appears in their **Projects** list. To include someone outside your company, invite them as a guest instead.

title: Remove a member from a project
aliases: revoke project access for a colleague
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the person in the **Members** list.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots) beside their name, then **Remove from project**.
4. Choose whether to **Reassign their open tasks** to another member or leave them unassigned.
5. Select **Remove**.
Their past comments and completed work stay in the project.

title: Change a member’s role in a project
body:
Roles control what each member can do in a project.
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the member in the list.
3. Select their current role, for example **Contributor**.
4. Choose **Manager**, **Contributor** or **Viewer**.
5. Select **Save**.
The change takes effect immediately.

title: Transfer project ownership
aliases: make someone else the project owner
body:
Each project has one owner who can delete it and manage billing codes.
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Under **General**, select the **Owner** field.
3. Choose a current **Manager** from the list.
4. Select **Transfer ownership**.
5. Confirm by selecting **Yes, transfer**.
You stay on the project as a **Manager**.

title: Set a project budget
aliases: add a budget to a project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Select **Budget**.
3. Choose **Budget type**: **Hours** or **Amount**.
4. Enter the budget figure and, for amounts, the **Currency**.
5. Select **Save changes**.
A progress bar appears on the **Overview** tab and turns amber when 80 per cent is used. Logged time updates it automatically.

title: Change a project’s colour and icon
aliases: pick a colour for a project
customise how a project looks in the sidebar
body:
Colours make projects easy to tell apart at a glance.
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Under **Appearance**, select the coloured square.
3. Choose a colour and an icon.
4. Select **Save changes**.
The new look shows in the sidebar, on the **Projects** page and on your board cards.

title: Filter the projects list
body:
1. Select **Projects** in the left sidebar.
2. Select **Filter** above the list.
3. Choose one or more conditions, such as **Status**, **Owner** or **Client**.
4. Select **Apply**.
5. To keep the filter for next time, select **Save view** and name it.
Select **Clear all** to see every project again. Use the search box to find a project by name.

title: Create a task
aliases: add a new task to a project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Select **Add task**.
3. Type the task name and press **Enter**.
4. Select the task to open its details.
5. Add an **Assignee**, **Due date** and **Description**.
Select **Save** if you changed any details. Tasks you create inside a column on the **Board** are placed in that column automatically.

title: Add a subtask to a task
aliases: break a task into smaller steps
create a checklist item under a task
body:
Subtasks split bigger jobs into steps that can each have an owner and due date.
1. Open the task.
2. Under **Subtasks**, select **Add subtask**.
3. Type a name and press **Enter**.
4. Repeat for each step.
The parent task shows progress, such as 2 of 5 complete. Subtasks can sit one level below a task only.

title: Assign a task to someone
aliases: give a task to a colleague
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Assignee** field.
3. Start typing a name and choose the person from the list.
4. To add more people, select **Add assignee**.
5. Close the task panel.
The person receives a notification. Only project members can be assigned tasks. Guests can be mentioned in comments but not assigned.

title: Change a task’s due date
aliases: move the deadline on a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Due date** field.
3. Choose the new date from the calendar, or select **Clear** to remove it.
4. Optionally add a time under **Due time**.
The assignee is notified of the change. If other tasks depend on this one, a prompt asks whether to move them as well.

title: Set a task’s priority
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Priority** field.
3. Choose **Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Urgent**.
Priority shows as a coloured flag on the task list and on board cards. You can sort the **Tasks** tab by priority by selecting the **Priority** column heading.

title: Change a task’s status
body:
Every task has a status that matches the columns on your board.
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Status** field.
3. Choose a status, such as **To do**, **In progress**, **Blocked** or **Done**.
On the **Board**, the card moves to the matching column straight away. Admins can rename statuses under **Settings**, then **Workflow**.

title: Mark a task as complete
body:
1. Find the task in the **Tasks** tab or on your **My tasks** page.
2. Select the circle to the left of the task name.
The circle turns green and the task moves to **Done**. If it has open subtasks, you will be asked whether to complete them too.
To complete a task from inside its details, select **Mark complete** at the top.

title: Reopen a completed task
aliases: mark done task as not done
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Select **Show completed** at the bottom of the list.
3. Open the task.
4. Select **Reopen task**.
5. Choose the status it should return to, such as **To do**.
The assignee is notified and the task reappears in the active list with its comments and files intact.

title: Add a label to a task
aliases: add a tag to a task
body:
Labels help you group and filter tasks across a project.
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Labels** field.
3. Choose an existing label, or type a new name and select **Create label**.
4. Press **Esc** to close the list.
You can add several labels to one task. Admins can edit or delete labels under **Settings**, then **Labels**.

title: Add a time estimate to a task
aliases: estimate how long a task will take
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Estimate** field.
3. Enter the time, for example **4h** or **1d 2h**.
4. Press **Enter**.
Estimates are added up on the **Overview** tab and compared with logged time in the **Reports** area. Subtask estimates roll up into the parent task.

title: Log time on a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Time** tab.
3. Select **Log time**.
4. Enter the **Duration**, the **Date** and an optional note.
5. Select **Save**.
You can also select **Start timer** and stop it when you finish. Time you log counts towards the project budget if one is set.

title: Delete a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top of the task panel.
3. Select **Delete task**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.
Deleted tasks go to the project’s **Trash** for 30 days, where a manager can restore them. Subtasks are deleted along with the parent.

title: Duplicate a task
aliases: make a copy of a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Duplicate task**.
4. Choose whether to include **Subtasks**, **Assignee** and **Attachments**.
5. Select **Duplicate**.
The copy is named with the word Copy at the end and appears in the same column or list.

title: Turn a subtask into a task
aliases: make a subtask its own task
body:
Use this when a step has grown into a job of its own.
1. Open the parent task.
2. Hover over the subtask under **Subtasks**.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Convert to task**.
The subtask becomes a task in the same project, keeping its assignee, due date and comments. It is no longer counted in the parent’s progress.

title: Move a task to another project
aliases: put task in a different project
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Move to project**.
3. Search for and select the destination project.
4. Choose a **Status** in that project.
5. Select **Move**.
Comments and files travel with the task. Assignees who are not members of the new project are removed from the task.

title: Make a task repeat
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Repeat** field.
3. Choose how often: **Daily**, **Weekly**, **Monthly** or **Custom**.
4. Pick an end: **Never** or **On a date**.
5. Select **Save**.
When someone completes the task, Harbour Projects creates the next one with the same assignee and a new due date.

title: Link a task that depends on another
aliases: make one task wait for another
body:
1. Open the task that has to wait.
2. Select **Dependencies**, then **Add dependency**.
3. Choose **Waiting on** and search for the other task.
4. Select **Add**.
The task shows a **Blocked** label until the one it is waiting on is complete. On the **Timeline**, an arrow connects the two bars.

title: Edit several tasks at once
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Tick the box beside each task you want to change.
3. Select **Edit selected** in the bar that appears.
4. Choose the field to change, such as **Assignee**, **Status** or **Due date**.
5. Enter the new value and select **Apply**.
You can edit up to 200 tasks at a time.

title: Export your tasks to CSV
aliases: download all my tasks to a spreadsheet
body:
1. In the left sidebar, select **My tasks**.
2. Select **Filter** to narrow the list, if needed.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Export to CSV**.
4. Select **Export**.
The CSV includes the task name, project, assignee, status and due date. To export one project only, use the export option on that project’s **Tasks** tab.

title: Import tasks from a CSV file
aliases: bring in tasks from a file
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Import from CSV**.
3. Select **Choose file** and pick your CSV.
4. Match each column in your file to a Harbour field, such as **Task name** and **Due date**.
5. Select **Import**.
Download the sample file first if you are unsure of the layout.

title: Add a column to a board
aliases: add a stage to my kanban board
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Scroll to the right-hand edge and select **Add column**.
3. Type a name, such as **In review**.
4. Press **Enter**.
New columns become statuses you can use on every task in the project. Drag the column by its heading to change where it sits.

title: Rename a board column
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top of the column.
3. Select **Rename**.
4. Type the new name and press **Enter**.
Tasks in the column keep their place, and their status updates to the new name.

title: Delete a board column
aliases: remove a column from the board
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top of the column.
3. Select **Delete column**.
4. Choose a column to **Move tasks to**.
5. Select **Delete**.
Tasks are never deleted with the column. Each one moves to the column you chose and takes on its status.

title: Set a work-in-progress limit on a column
body:
A limit helps your team finish work before starting more.
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) on the column.
3. Select **Set limit**.
4. Enter the maximum number of cards.
5. Select **Save**.
The column count turns red when the limit is exceeded. Cards can still be added, so the limit acts as a warning.

title: Move a card between columns
aliases: drag a card to another column
change a task’s stage on the board
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Click and hold the card.
3. Drag it to the new column and release.
To move a card without dragging, open it, select the **Status** field and choose the column name. The task’s status updates to match, and the assignee is notified if the new status is **Done**.

title: Collapse a column
aliases: hide a column on the board
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select the small arrow at the top left of the column heading.
The column folds into a narrow strip showing only its name and card count. Select the arrow again to expand it.
Your choice is remembered for you only. It does not change the board for other members.

title: Filter the cards on a board
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select **Filter** at the top of the board.
3. Choose conditions such as **Assignee**, **Label**, **Priority** or **Due date**.
4. Select **Apply**.
A blue dot on the **Filter** button shows a filter is active. Select **Clear all** to see every card again.

title: Group a board into swimlanes
body:
Swimlanes add horizontal rows so you can see each person’s work across all columns.
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select **Group by** at the top of the board.
3. Choose **Assignee**, **Priority** or **Label**.
Select **None** to return to a single row. Rows can be collapsed with the arrow beside each name.

title: Choose what shows on board cards
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select **Card settings**, shown as a small sliders icon.
3. Tick or untick the fields to show, such as **Due date**, **Assignee**, **Labels** and **Subtask progress**.
4. Select **Done**.
This setting applies to everyone using the board and needs a **Manager** role.

title: Change a card’s colour
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Hover over the card and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Card colour**.
4. Choose a colour.
The colour appears as a stripe along the card’s left edge. To colour every card by priority or label instead, use **Colour by** in the board’s **Card settings**.

title: Archive completed cards
body:
Archiving keeps a long board tidy without losing any work.
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) on the **Done** column.
3. Select **Archive all cards**.
4. Select **Archive** to confirm.
Tasks remain in the project and can be found under **Show completed** on the **Tasks** tab.

title: Save a board view
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab and set up your filters and grouping.
2. Select **Views** at the top of the board.
3. Select **Save current view**.
4. Enter a name, such as **My open work**.
5. Choose **Only me** or **Everyone in project**.
6. Select **Save**.
Saved views appear in the **Views** list for quick switching.

title: Switch from the board to the timeline
aliases: see my project as a gantt chart
body:
1. Open the project.
2. Select the **Timeline** tab.
Each task with a start and due date appears as a bar. Tasks without dates are listed in the **Unscheduled** panel on the left.
Your filters from the **Board** are carried across, so you see the same set of tasks.

title: Zoom the timeline in or out
aliases: see the whole project on one screen
body:
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Select **Zoom** at the top right.
3. Choose **Days**, **Weeks**, **Months** or **Quarters**.
Select **Fit to project** to scale the timeline so the whole project is visible. You can also hold **Ctrl** and scroll your mouse wheel.

title: Reschedule a task on the timeline
aliases: drag task bar to new dates
change start and end date on the gantt
shift a task on the timeline
body:
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Drag a task bar left or right to move both dates.
3. Drag the left or right edge of the bar to change only the start date or due date.
4. Release to save.
Tasks linked by a dependency move together if you tick **Move dependent tasks** at the top of the timeline.

title: Add a milestone to the timeline
body:
Milestones mark key dates, such as a client sign-off or launch.
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Select **Add**, then **Milestone**.
3. Enter a **Name** and choose a **Date**.
4. Select **Create**.
A diamond appears on the timeline. You can drag it to a new date or link tasks to it so it moves when they do.

title: Show or hide dependency arrows
body:
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Select **Display** at the top of the timeline.
3. Switch **Dependencies** on or off.
With arrows on, any task that runs late is outlined in red. Switch dependencies off if the timeline looks cluttered. This only changes your own view.

title: Save a baseline on the timeline
body:
A baseline captures your current plan so you can see how far work has slipped.
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Select **Baseline**, then **Save baseline**.
3. Name the baseline, for example **Kick-off plan**.
4. Select **Save**.
Grey bars appear under each task showing the original dates. Only **Managers** can save or delete baselines.

title: Export the timeline as a PDF
body:
1. Open the **Timeline** tab and choose the zoom level you want.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top right.
3. Select **Export as PDF**.
4. Choose a **Page size** and **Orientation**.
5. Select **Export**.
The PDF shows what is on screen, including any filters, so clear them first if you want every task.

title: Add a client
body:
1. In the left sidebar, select **Clients**.
2. Select **New client**.
3. Enter the **Client name**.
4. Add a **Primary contact**, **Email** and **Phone**.
5. Select **Save client**.
You can link projects to the client afterwards. Clients are kept separate from your team, so adding one does not use a user seat.

title: Update a client’s phone number
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. On the **Details** tab, select **Edit**.
4. Update the **Phone** field.
5. Select **Save**.
The new number shows on the client page and on any project linked to that client. Previous numbers are not kept.

title: Update a client’s email address
aliases: new email for a client contact
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. On the **Details** tab, select **Edit**.
4. Change the **Email** field.
5. Select **Save**.
Notifications to the client contact are sent to the new address from now on. If the contact is also a guest, update their sign-in email separately from the **People** tab.

title: Delete a client
body:
Only account admins can delete clients.
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Delete client**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.
Linked projects are not deleted. They simply lose their client. If you want to keep the record, set the client to inactive instead.

title: Mark a client as inactive
aliases: hide a client I no longer work with
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. Select the **Status** field and choose **Inactive**.
4. Select **Save**.
Inactive clients are hidden from the default **Clients** list and cannot be chosen for new projects. Select **Filter**, then **Inactive** to find them again.

title: Merge duplicate clients
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Tick the two records you want to combine.
3. Select **Merge**.
4. Choose which record to keep as the main one.
5. Review the fields and select **Merge clients**.
Projects, notes and guests from both records move to the one you kept. A merge cannot be undone.

title: Add a billing contact to a client
aliases: new billing person for a customer
body:
The billing contact receives budget and time reports if you share them.
1. Open the client from **Clients**.
2. Select the **Contacts** tab.
3. Select **Add contact**.
4. Enter their name, email and phone.
5. Tick **Billing contact**.
6. Select **Save**.

title: Change a client’s billing contact
body:
1. Open the client from **Clients**.
2. Select the **Contacts** tab.
3. Find the contact you want to make the billing contact.
4. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Make billing contact**.
5. Select **Confirm**.
The previous billing contact stays on the client as a regular contact. A client can have only one billing contact at a time.

title: Add a note to a client
aliases: record a call with a client
log a conversation with a customer
body:
Notes are visible to your team only. Clients and guests never see them.
1. Open the client from **Clients**.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Select **Add note**.
4. Type your note. You can mention a teammate with @.
5. Select **Save note**.
Notes are listed with the newest first and show who wrote them.

title: Link a project to a client
aliases: assign a client to a project
set the client for a project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Under **General**, select the **Client** field.
3. Search for and choose the client.
4. Select **Save changes**.
The project now appears on the client’s **Projects** tab. You can invite that client’s contacts as guests from the **People** tab.

title: See all projects for a client
aliases: find work done for a customer
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. Select the **Projects** tab.
The list shows every project linked to the client, with its status, owner and due date. Select **Show archived** to include finished work. Select a project name to open it.

title: Export your clients to CSV
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Use **Filter** if you only need some clients.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Export to CSV**.
4. Choose the columns to include, such as **Client name**, **Email**, **Phone** and **Status**.
5. Select **Export**.
The file downloads straight away. Only admins and managers can export clients.

title: Import clients from a CSV file
aliases: bring clients in from a spreadsheet
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Import from CSV**.
3. Select **Choose file**.
4. Match your columns to fields such as **Client name** and **Email**.
5. Select **Import**.
Rows with an email that already exists are skipped and listed in a summary you can download.

title: Set a client’s default hourly rate
aliases: set billing rate for a customer
add a rate to a client
body:
1. Open the client from **Clients**.
2. Select the **Billing** tab.
3. Select **Edit rates**.
4. Enter the **Hourly rate** and choose the **Currency**.
5. Select **Save**.
New projects linked to this client use the rate by default. Existing projects keep their current rate unless you change it in the project’s **Budget** settings.

title: Invite a guest to a project
aliases: give a client access to a project
share a project with an outsider
body:
Guests are people outside your company, such as clients, who can see only the projects you share.
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Select **Invite guest**.
3. Enter their email address.
4. Choose a **Permission**: **Can view**, **Can comment** or **Can approve**.
5. Select **Send invite**.

title: Resend a guest invitation
body:
Invitations expire after 14 days.
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the guest under **Pending invites**.
3. Select **Resend invite**.
A fresh email goes to the guest with a new link. If it still does not arrive, ask them to check their spam folder, or correct the address by removing the guest and inviting them again.

title: Change a guest’s permission
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the guest under **Guests**.
3. Select their current permission.
4. Choose **Can view**, **Can comment** or **Can approve**.
5. Select **Save**.
Guests on **Can comment** can add comments but cannot edit tasks. Guests on **Can approve** can also approve tasks marked **Needs approval**.

title: Remove a guest from a project
aliases: stop sharing project with someone outside
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the guest under **Guests**.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Remove guest**.
4. Select **Remove** to confirm.
The guest can no longer open the project. Their comments stay in place. If they are a guest on other projects, those are not affected.

title: Set an end date for a guest’s access
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the guest under **Guests**.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Set access end date**.
4. Choose a date.
5. Select **Save**.
Harbour Projects emails the guest and the project owner seven days before access ends. After that, the guest cannot open the project.

title: Choose what guests are emailed about
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Select **Guest notifications**.
3. Tick the events guests should hear about, such as **Status updates**, **New comments** and **Files shared**.
4. Select **Save changes**.
This applies to all guests on the project. Guests can still turn off emails for themselves from their own profile.

title: Upload a file to a project
aliases: put a file in the project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Select **Upload**.
3. Choose one or more files from your computer, or drag them onto the page.
4. Wait for the progress bar to finish.
Each file can be up to 500 MB. To attach a file to one task instead, open the task and select **Attach file** under **Attachments**.

title: Upload a new version of a file
aliases: replace a file with an updated one
add version two of a file
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Upload new version**.
4. Choose the updated file.
5. Add a short **Version note**, then select **Upload**.
The name and any comments stay the same. Earlier versions are kept in the file’s history.

title: Download a file
aliases: save a file to my computer
get a copy of an attachment
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Find the file, or open the task it is attached to.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots) beside the file.
4. Select **Download**.
The latest version downloads to your browser’s usual folder. To download older versions, open the file’s **Version history**.

title: Download all project files as a zip
aliases: get everything in the Files tab
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Select **Select all**, or tick individual files and folders.
3. Select **Download** at the top of the list.
4. Wait for the zip to be prepared.
Large downloads can take a few minutes. Harbour Projects emails you a download link if the zip is bigger than 1 GB.

title: Rename a file
aliases: edit the name of a document
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Rename**.
4. Type the new name. Keep the file extension, such as .pdf.
5. Press **Enter**.
The new name shows wherever the file is attached, including in tasks and comments.

title: Create a folder for files
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Select **New folder**.
3. Type a name, for example **Signed contracts**.
4. Press **Enter**.
To put files inside, drag them onto the folder, or use **Move to folder** from the file’s **More** menu. Folders can be nested up to five levels deep.

title: Move a file into a folder
aliases: put a file in a different folder
body:
1. Open the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Move to folder**.
4. Choose the destination folder, or select **New folder** to make one.
5. Select **Move**.
You can also drag a file onto a folder in the list.

title: Delete a file
aliases: remove a file from a project
body:
1. Open the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete file** to confirm.
All versions of the file are moved to **Trash**. They are removed for good after 30 days. Removing an attachment from a task also deletes the file from the project.

title: Restore a deleted file
aliases: get a file back from trash
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Select **Trash** at the top of the page.
3. Find the file. Use the search box if the list is long.
4. Select **Restore**.
The file returns to its original folder with its comments and versions. Files in **Trash** for more than 30 days cannot be recovered.

title: Restore an earlier version of a file
aliases: go back to an old version
body:
1. Open the **Files** tab and select the file.
2. Select **Version history** in the side panel.
3. Find the version you need. Each shows who uploaded it and when.
4. Select **Restore this version**.
5. Select **Restore** to confirm.
The restored copy becomes the newest version. Nothing is overwritten, so the other versions stay in the list.

title: Choose whether guests can see a file
aliases: make a file visible to guests
body:
New files are visible to guests by default.
1. Open the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Visibility**.
4. Choose **Team only** or **Team and guests**.
5. Select **Save**.
A small lock icon marks files that are team only.

title: Add a comment to a task
aliases: leave a message on a task
post an update on a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the box labelled **Add a comment** at the bottom of the panel.
3. Type your message.
4. To include a file, select the paperclip icon.
5. Select **Send**.
Assignees and watchers are notified. Press **Ctrl+Enter** (**Cmd+Enter** on Mac) to send faster.

title: Edit a comment
aliases: fix a typo in a comment
body:
1. Open the task and find your comment.
2. Hover over it and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Change the text.
5. Select **Save**.
An **Edited** label appears beside the time. You can edit your own comments at any time, but not other people’s.

title: Delete a comment
aliases: erase a message on a task
body:
1. Open the task and find the comment.
2. Hover over it and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete comment** to confirm.
You can delete your own comments. **Managers** can delete anyone’s comment in their project. Replies stay in place and show a note that the original was removed.

title: Mention someone in a comment
aliases: notify a teammate in a comment
body:
1. Open the task and select the **Add a comment** box.
2. Type @ followed by the person’s name.
3. Choose them from the list that appears.
4. Finish your comment and select **Send**.
The person gets an email and an in-app notification, even if they are not watching the task. If they are not a member of the project, you will be asked whether to add them.

title: Reply to a comment
aliases: reply to someone on a task
body:
Replies keep related messages together.
1. Open the task and find the comment.
2. Select **Reply** beneath it.
3. Type your response.
4. Select **Send**.
Replies appear indented under the original comment. The person you reply to is notified automatically.

title: Resolve a comment thread
body:
Resolving tells everyone the feedback has been dealt with.
1. Open the task or file and find the thread.
2. Select **Resolve** at the top of the first comment.
The thread collapses and moves to **Resolved**. To reopen it, select **Resolved comments**, find the thread and select **Reopen**.

title: Make a comment visible to the team only
body:
Use internal comments for discussion you do not want guests to read.
1. Open the task and select the **Add a comment** box.
2. Select the **Visible to** drop-down below the box.
3. Choose **Team only**.
4. Type your message and select **Send**.
A padlock marks internal comments. The setting cannot be changed after sending, so delete and repost if you chose wrongly.

title: Attach a file to a comment
aliases: add a document to a message
send a file with my comment
include a screenshot in a comment
body:
1. Open the task and select the **Add a comment** box.
2. Select the paperclip icon.
3. Choose a file from your computer, or drag one into the box.
4. Type your message.
5. Select **Send**.
The file also appears on the project’s **Files** tab. To paste a screenshot, copy it and press **Ctrl+V** in the comment box.

title: Turn off email notifications for comments
body:
1. Select your profile picture at the top right, then **Notification settings**.
2. Under **Comments**, switch off **Email me about new comments**.
3. Select **Save**.
You will still see comments in your in-app **Inbox**. To mute a single task, open it and select **Unwatch**.

title: Print a board
aliases: get a paper copy of the board
save board as PDF to print
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Apply any filters you want to appear on the printout.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top right.
4. Select **Print board**.
5. Choose a **Page size** and select **Print**.
Only cards that match your current filters are included. Archived cards are never printed.
